question: Which missile was showcased and launched during Republic Day, 2025?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Pralay**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Pralay** missile was one of the major highlights showcased during the **76th Republic Day Parade** held on **January 26, 2025**, at **Kartavya Path** in **New Delhi**.
 
• It is a **surface-to-surface**, **short-range ballistic missile (SRBM)** specifically developed for battlefield use to provide the **Indian Army** with a tactical edge.
 
• The missile has been developed by the **Defence Research and Development Organisation (DRDO)** and represents a shift in India’s defense strategy toward a dedicated **Rocket Force**.
 
• The **Pralay** missile has a strike **range** of **150 km to 500 km**, making it effective for neutralizing high-value enemy targets like radar installations, command centers, and airfields.
 
• The missile is powered by a **solid-propellant rocket motor** and follows a **quasi-ballistic trajectory**, which allows it to maneuver in flight to evade interceptor missiles. ***Hence, the statement regarding its display in 2025 is correct.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Missile Capabilities and Features:**

 
 
• **Pralay** is a **canisterized missile**, which means it can be stored for long periods and launched quickly from mobile launchers, providing high operational **flexibility**.
 
• It carries a **payload** of **350 kg to 700 kg**, including high explosives and submunitions, designed to destroy hardened targets.
 
• The missile’s **guidance system** includes state-of-the-art **navigation** and integrated **avionics** to ensure high precision during the terminal phase of the flight.
 
 
 
• **Comparison with Global Systems:**
 
 
• Military experts often compare **Pralay** to Russia’s **Iskander** missile and China’s **Dongfeng-12** due to its ability to fly at low altitudes and change its path mid-air.
 
• Its induction is a part of India's plan to create a **Integrated Rocket Force** to counter threats along the **Line of Actual Control (LAC)** and **Line of Control (LoC)**.
 
 
 
• **Other Missiles in the Options:**
 
 
• **Nirbhay:** It is India’s first indigenous **long-range subsonic cruise missile** with a range of **1000 km**, capable of carrying nuclear and conventional warheads.
 
• **Agni-V:** An **Intercontinental Ballistic Missile (ICBM)** with a range exceeding **5000 km**, forming the backbone of India’s nuclear deterrence.
 
• **Brahmos NG:** A "Next Generation" smaller, lighter version of the **Brahmos supersonic cruise missile**, designed for deployment on various fighter aircraft like the **Sukhoi-30 MKI** and **LCA Tejas**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Development Timeline:** The **DRDO** conducted the first successful flight test of **Pralay** in **December 2021** at **Abdul Kalam Island**, off the coast of **Odisha**.
 
• **Strategic Significance:** The mass production and induction of **Pralay** signify **India's** move toward self-reliance in **defense technology** (**Atmanirbhar Bharat**) and strengthening tactical conventional strike capabilities.
 
• **Modern Warfare:** In modern conflicts, **Short-Range Ballistic Missiles** like **Pralay** are essential for **non-nuclear** strikes where precision is more important than massive destruction.
